title: Head of Engineering - Quilter
description:
About the Business

Quilter plc is a leading wealth management business, helping to enable brighter financial futures for every generation. Quilter oversees £141.9 billion in customer investments (as of March 2026). It has an adviser and customer offering spanning financial advice, investment platforms, multi-asset investment solutions, and discretionary fund management. The business is comprised of two segments: Affluent and High Net Worth.

Affluent encompasses the financial planning business, Quilter Financial Planning, the Quilter Investment Platform and Quilter Investors, the multi-asset investment solutions business. High Net Worth includes the discretionary fund management business, Quilter Cheviot, together with Quilter Cheviot Financial Planning - offering a highly personalised service to private clients, charities, trustees, and professional partners. Quilter Cheviot has presence throughout the UK, Ireland and Channel Islands.

At Quilter we never stand still. Our foundations are rooted in our extraordinary expertise, which is trusted by hundreds of thousands of customers, but we have great ambitions to stay one step ahead and make an even greater difference to the people and communities we serve, including our colleagues.

Our business is transforming, continually modernising, and becoming even more customer centric. So, if you want to be bold in the pursuit of your ambitions, bring new ideas, and challenge and evolve what we do, it's the perfect time to join us!

About the Role

As the Head of Engineering, you will be the enterprise owner of the engineering capability. The role is accountable for ensuring that the organisation's technology platforms, regardless of buy or built are delivered to a consistently high engineering standard that is defined and governed within the engineering practice.

You will report to the CTDO and act as a senior technology partner to business, product, change, architecture, infrastructure, information security, data, operations and third-party delivery partners. The role requires strong functional and technical leadership, and stakeholder influence across a regulated environment

The role is required to build the quality engineering practice, DevSecOps enablement, engineering standards, tooling, career frameworks and the safe adoption of AI-assisted software delivery.

Key responsibilities

  • Define and execute the engineering strategy aligned to business, technology and product priorities
  • Establish the engineering operating model, including team struc#
  • tures, accountabilities, ways of working and decision rights aligned with the broader ways of working for Quilter
  • Provide technical leadership across the engineering teams and ensure appropriate engineering governance that is light touch and ensures execution at pace is not compromised.
  • Maintain awareness of emerging technology and engineering trends and translate to meaningful and purposeful conversations and initiatives that drive business value
  • Build and lead a high-performing Engineering organisation, creating a culture of technical excellence, accountability, innovation, continuous improvement and customer focus.
  • Define and evolve Quilter's engineering strategy, ensuring engineering investments, capabilities and practices support business priorities, customer outcomes and long-term technology goals.
  • Establish and continuously improve engineering standards covering software design, coding, quality engineering, integration, deployment and production stability. Lead the evolution of engineering enablement capabilities, including platform engineering, developer tooling, automation and self-service engineering services, reducing friction and improving the effectiveness of software delivery teams.
  • Continuously improve developer experience (DevEx) by providing engineers with the tools, environments, processes and support required to build, test, deploy and operate software efficiently and safely. Use DORA or complimentary engineering metrics to understand delivery performance and engineering productivity.
  • Establish and evolve the platform engineering capability that enables engineering teams to build, test, deploy and operate software through self service or SDK (self development kit)
  • Partner with Enterprise and Solution Architecture to ensure engineering decisions support the organisation's target architecture by attending ARB and ensuring that architectural decisions are cascaded to the engineering communities. Promote modular, API and event driven architectures.
  • Drive the evolution of Quality Engineering, embedding quality throughout the software development lifecycle through automation, performance engineering, test data management, production feedback loops and shared accountability for quality outcomes. Establish quality gates and automated controls throughout the software development life cycle.
  • Define and lead the organisation's strategy for AI assisted software engineering. Enable engineers to safely use AI coding assistants. Establish appropriate governance for AI generated code.
  • Develop engineering practices that move teams from AI coding assistants towards effective human + AI workflows
  • Drive modern software engineering practices by owning and continuously enhance DevSecOps capabilities, including CI/CD, automated testing, infrastructure as a code, API first development and secure software development.
  • Build a culture of small, frequent, safe releases rather than large, high risk release deployments
  • Embed security throughout the engineering lifecycle, implement automated security controls within CI/CD pipelines including code scanning and vulnerability management. Establish secure coding practices and engineering security standards. Work with the cyber security team to implement security policies and practices.
  • Establish clear engineering accountability with you build it you run concept
  • Balance internal and external delivery capabilities, ensuring the organisation has the right mix of skills, capacity, succession planning and commercial oversight to meet evolving business demand.

title: Production Assistant
description:
Join Our Growing Team – New Mississauga Location!

Wholesome Kids Catering is excited to announce the opening of our new location in Mississauga!

Wholesome Kids Catering is a leading provider of nutritious, delicious, and thoughtfully prepared meals and snacks for childcare centres and schools. Our team is committed to food safety, exceptional service, and creating healthy meals that children love.

Join Wholesome Kids Catering and become part of One Team One Dream as we deliver healthy food and exceptional service—one meal at a time!

Position Information

Position Title: Production Associate (PA) – Mississauga
Reports To: Production Supervisor
Direct Reports: None
Available Shifts: 5:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m. and 1:00 p.m.–9:00 p.m.
Vacation: Two weeks of vacation per year plus five paid Wellness Days

Flexibility may be required to support operational needs, training, production demands, audits, special projects, and coverage across shifts.

The Role

As a Production Associate, you will contribute to the daily production of thousands of nutritious meals and snacks in a fast-paced, high-volume food manufacturing and commissary kitchen environment.

You will work collaboratively with Production Leads, Supervisors, and fellow team members to ensure products are prepared, assembled, packaged, labelled, staged, and distributed safely and efficiently. You will help ensure that every product meets Wholesome Kids Catering’s food safety, quality, accuracy, and customer service standards before it leaves our facility.

Key Responsibilities

Production Operations

  • Assemble meals, snacks, and meal components according to daily production schedules, work instructions, production plans, recipes, and customer specifications.
  • Accurately count, portion, weigh, sort, assemble, label, and package products while maintaining established quality and quantity standards.
  • Verify product quantities, production labels, packaging materials, route information, and customer orders to ensure accuracy before distribution.
  • Pack meals and snacks efficiently while maintaining product quality, presentation, packaging integrity, and temperature-control standards.
  • Organize and stage completed products for shipping according to route schedules, customer requirements, and delivery timelines.
  • Replenish ingredients, labels, packaging materials, containers, and other supplies to support a continuous and efficient production workflow.
  • Safely transport products, ingredient bins, rolling racks, carts, pallets, and production materials throughout the facility.
  • Rotate between production areas and workstations based on daily schedules, operational requirements, and production priorities.
  • Assist with inventory movement, product transfers, and stock replenishment while maintaining product traceability and inventory accuracy.
  • Process returned products according to company procedures, document discrepancies, and escalate concerns when required.
  • Maintain accurate production records, counts, labels, checklists, and other required documentation.
  • Consistently work toward daily production targets while maintaining exceptional quality, accuracy, efficiency, and attention to detail.

Food Safety, Quality and Compliance

  • Follow all Standard Operating Procedures, Good Manufacturing Practices, HACCP requirements, allergen-control procedures, and company food safety policies.
  • Maintain high standards of cleanliness, personal hygiene, sanitation, and safe food handling throughout all production activities.
  • Verify that products meet company requirements for appearance, portion size, weight, packaging, labelling, quality, temperature, and order accuracy.
  • Recognize and immediately report quality concerns, product defects, packaging issues, contamination risks, equipment malfunctions, shortages, and production delays.
  • Follow colour-coding, utensil-control, handwashing, glove-changing, and sanitation requirements when moving between products or production areas.
  • Maintain product traceability by accurately completing production records, batch documentation, temperature logs, product counts, and operational checklists.
  • Follow FIFO—First In, First Out—inventory rotation procedures to minimize waste and support product quality and freshness.
  • Protect ingredients and finished products from contamination, damage, temperature abuse, incorrect labelling, or unauthorized use.

Equipment and Material Handling

  • Safely operate production equipment, scales, label printers, packaging equipment, rolling racks, carts, pallet jacks where trained, and other authorized production tools.
  • Inspect equipment and tools before use and immediately report damage, defects, missing guards, or unsafe operating conditions.
  • Use equipment only after receiving the required training and authorization.
  • Handle products, ingredients, packaging materials, tools, and equipment carefully to prevent damage, contamination, product loss, or workplace injury.
  • Assist with equipment setup, cleaning, disassembly, and basic operational care according to established procedures and manufacturer instructions.

Teamwork and Operational Excellence

  • Work collaboratively with Production Leads, Supervisors, Warehouse, Quality Assurance, Sanitation, Logistics, and other Operations team members to achieve daily goals.
  • Communicate production updates, shortages, quality concerns, equipment issues, and operational challenges promptly and professionally.
  • Demonstrate flexibility by supporting multiple production lines, workstations, and operational areas based on business requirements.
  • Follow instructions and respond positively to changing production priorities, customer needs, menu changes, and scheduling requirements.
  • Support the onboarding and cross-training of new Production Associates when assigned.
  • Share relevant information during shift transitions to support continuity, accountability, and efficient production.
  • Maintain a positive attitude and contribute to a respectful, inclusive, collaborative, and team-oriented work environment.
  • Take ownership of assigned duties and follow through on commitments.

Health, Safety and Housekeeping

  • Comply with applicable workplace health and safety legislation, company policies, procedures, and safe work practices.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free workstation by following clean-as-you-go principles throughout the shift.
  • Clean and sanitize work surfaces, tools, containers, and equipment according to established procedures.
  • Immediately report unsafe conditions, near misses, hazards, injuries, incidents, spills, damaged equipment, and food safety concerns to the Production Lead or Supervisor.
  • Wear and properly maintain all required personal protective equipment.
  • Follow food manufacturing hygiene requirements, including handwashing, hair and beard restraints, protective clothing, footwear, and restrictions concerning jewellery or personal items.
  • Use appropriate lifting, pushing, pulling, and material-handling techniques to prevent injury.
  • Follow emergency procedures and cooperate with incident investigations, corrective actions, and safety training.
  • Perform all duties safely while protecting coworkers, visitors, equipment, and the integrity of the products we produce.

Physical and Environmental Requirements

  • Lift and carry materials weighing up to 60 pounds.
  • Stand and walk for extended periods during the shift.
  • Frequently bend, reach, twist, push, pull, lift, and carry.
  • Perform repetitive tasks requiring consistent speed, coordination, and attention to detail.
  • Work in refrigerated environments with temperatures of approximately 4–10°C.
  • Work around industrial kitchen equipment, moving carts, production machinery, noise, food products, and cleaning activities.
  • Safely use authorized food preparation tools and production equipment.
  • Push and move rolling racks, ingredient carts, pallets, and production equipment.
  • Operate a pallet jack when appropriately trained and authorized.
  • Maintain concentration, accuracy, and awareness in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
  • Work safely around common food allergens while following established allergen-control procedures.

Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or equivalent is preferred.
  • Previous experience in food manufacturing, catering, institutional food service, commercial kitchens, packaging, warehousing, or high-volume production is considered an asset.
  • Basic understanding of food safety, sanitation, and safe food handling is preferred.
  • Ability to read and follow production sheets, labels, work instructions, schedules, and safety procedures.
  • Ability to work independently while also contributing positively within a team.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and product accuracy.
  • Ability to follow verbal and written instructions.
  • Ability to communicate concerns and production updates clearly and professionally.
  • Reliable attendance and punctuality.
  • Ability to work the assigned shift and demonstrate flexibility when operational needs change.

Success Profile

A successful Production Associate consistently helps produce safe, nutritious, accurate, and high-quality meals while supporting efficient daily operations.

They demonstrate adaptability by moving confidently between production, assembly, packaging, labelling, staging, and sanitation-related tasks. They take ownership of their work, communicate concerns promptly, support their coworkers, and remain focused during busy production periods.

Most importantly, they understand that every meal represents a promise to the children, families, childcare centres, and schools we serve. They help ensure that every product meets Wholesome Kids Catering’s food safety, quality, and accuracy standards before it leaves our facility

title: Payer Access Cell Therapy Director
description:
Work with us
Our team are passionate in the pursuit of excellence and in pushing the boundaries of cancer therapy and Autoimmune disease to deliver life-changing treatments to patients.

Whilst working at Autolus you will enjoy a flexible, diverse and dynamic working environment which actively promotes creativity, leadership and teamwork – together we are ONE Autolus.

Job Description:

Job Title: Director, Payer Access Cell Therapy (PACT)

Reports to: VP US Head of Market Access

Department: Commercial

Hours: Full Time

Location: U.S., Remote

About Autolus

Autolus is a biopharmaceutical company, advancing innovative therapies at both clinical and commercial stages of development, focused on next-generation, programmed T cell therapies for the treatment of cancer. Using a broad suite of proprietary and modular T cell programming technologies, the company is engineering precisely targeted, controlled, and highly active T cell therapies designed to better recognize cancer cells, break down their defence mechanisms, and eliminate these cells. Autolus has a pipeline of product candidates in development for the treatment of haematological malignancies, solid tumours, and autoimmune diseases.

Why Autolus

Our team is passionate in the pursuit of excellence and in pushing the boundaries of cancer therapy to deliver life-changing treatments to patients. Whilst working at Autolus you will enjoy a flexible, diverse, and dynamic working environment which actively promotes creativity, leadership and teamwork. In addition to this Autolus is proud to offer a competitive salary, performance related bonus as well as private medical insurance, life assurance, pension and access to an employee share scheme. Autolus promotes flexible working.

Our Promise

Autolus is developing complex, breakthrough therapies for a globally diverse market and equally recognises that diversity amongst our people is critical to our mission. As we draw on our differences, what we’ve experienced, and how we work, we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees

Role Summary

This role will be covering the Central/North East area. The Director, Payer Access Cell Therapy will be an integral member of the commercial organization, focused on operationalizing the overall Market Access strategy, and ensuring patients have timely access to Autolus therapies. The primary objective of the Director, Payer Access Cell Therapy is to secure robust coverage and reimbursement for all Autolus products through regional, national, and government payers. In collaboration with center engagement and account management, this role will be integral to onboarding treatment centers and supporting broad timely patient access. The Director, Payer Access Cell Therapy will be a thought leader on all access related items including payer policy, pricing communication, and treatment center reimbursement.

Key Responsibilities

  • Identify, develop, and manage strategic relationships with National / Regional Commercial and Government payers within assigned geography.
  • Implement approved pre-launch payer education plan to ensure awareness of Autolus pipeline and prepare the payer market for new cell therapy entrants.
  • Present / provide approved product education and health economic information to key customers and communicate the value proposition of Autolus products.
  • Assess payer and policy landscape to understand and plan for potential coverage of Autolus products for Commercial, Medicare and Medicaid patients, including policy legislation, payer class management, and advocacy.
  • Obtain coverage for Autolus products within assigned accounts, while also identifying and mitigating potential challenges that may hinder access.
  • Partner with Medical Affairs and Global Market Access team to address clinical and outcomes concerns from payers.
  • Working knowledge of total cost of care and all aspects of reimbursement (coding, coverage, and payment) for inpatient and outpatient settings across payer segments.
  • Understand payer requirements and hospital reimbursement for cell therapies administered in the inpatient setting, including CMS requirements and implications for new novel therapies.
  • Inform and educate authorized treatment centers on coverage, billing, coding, and reimbursement of Autolus cell therapies.
  • Work with Autolus Patient Support to ensure understanding of payer coverage policies and requirements and assist with any coverage questions.
  • Responsible and accountable for the successful implementation within geography of the strategic and tactical market access plan.
  • Post launch, partner with field account management team to provide education on respective payers and to address any questions or concerns that arise.

Demonstrated Skills and Competencies

Experience

  • Demonstrated successful experience with National and Regional payers in Commercial, Medicaid, and Medicare.
  • Sustained track record of access and reimbursement achievement in cell therapy, gene therapy, or hematology / oncology.
  • Excellent strategic and business acumen skills, with demonstrated ability to successfully partner with payers.
  • Knowledge of medical benefit along with inpatient and outpatient economics preferred.
  • Extensive experience with private and public payers, across all settings of care, to include the economic complexities for reimbursement in each setting.
  • Extensive understanding of hematology / oncology clinical landscape, and the business of cell therapy.
  • Strong ability to work collaboratively and cross-functionally to ensure goals are achieved.
  • Possess a willingness and ability to work hands-on and with a sense of urgency, in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
  • Experience in onboarding cell therapies with treatment centers highly preferred.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher and 10+ years hematology / oncology experience in payer relations and market access.

Skills/Specialist Knowledge

  • Deep knowledge of CART/Cell Therapy access, reimbursement, and policy dynamics.
  • In-depth therapeutic and clinical knowledge in hematologic malignancies.
  • Strong ability to work cross-functionally in a dynamic, fast paced environment.
  • Routinely synthesizes customer information into actionable insights & recommendations.
  • Proven leadership experience and capabilities.
  • Recognized role model of Autolus core values and ways of working that inspire high performance culture and engagement.
  • Ability to problem solve, demonstrate flexibility, and think strategically.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills with the ability to effectively present to and engage with a wide range of audiences.
  • Proficient in PowerPoint, excel and word.
  • Resilient in high-pressure environments.

Travel Required: Approximately 50%

The anticipated annual base salary range for this position is $194,000 - $260,000

Actual compensation will be determined based on a number of factors, including relevant experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, and internal equity considerations.

Autolus Core Competencies

Focus on Results: Works to meet business goals set by management and leaders

Builds Trust and Relationships: Ensures trust with internal and external partners by delivering on commitments

Resilience: Has the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness

Communicates and Collaborates: Builds partnerships and works collaboratively with others to meet objectives

description:
Welcome! We’re excited you’re considering an opportunity with us! To apply to this position and be considered, click the Apply button located above this message and complete the application in full. Below, you’ll find other important information about this position.

Serves as lead responsible for monitoring, maintaining and coordinating work assignments. Performs ongoing audits of select inpatients and outpatient accounts and provides training to ensure optimum reimbursement and hospital coding compliance. Ensures accurate and appropriate information is documented, coded, and entered into the system(s) in order to meet departmental, hospital and outside agency requirements. This includes appropriate reimbursement, verification, compliance, and charging with the various coding guidelines and regulatory agencies. Responsible for obtaining accurate and complete documentation in the medical record for accurate coding assignment, severity of illness and risk of mortality for each medical record.

About Us At ExxonMobil, our vision is to lead in energy innovations that advance modern living and a net-zero future. As one of the world's largest publicly traded energy and chemical companies, we are powered by a unique and diverse workforce fueled by the pride in what we do and what we stand for.

The success of our Upstream, Product Solutions and Low Carbon Solutions businesses is the result of the talent, curiosity and drive of our people. They bring solutions every day to optimize our strategy in energy, chemicals, lubricants and lower-emissions technologies.

We invite you to bring your ideas to ExxonMobil to help create sustainable solutions that improve quality of life and meet society's evolving needs. Learn more about our What and our Why and how we can work together.

ExxonMobil in Singapore

ExxonMobil is one of Singapore's largest foreign manufacturing investors with over S$25 billion in fixed asset investments.

We have manufacturing facilities that include an integrated world-scale refining and petrochemical complex in Jurong and Jurong Island, a network of service stations under the Esso brand, operate a lubricant plant and are a supplier of cylinder cooking gas. ExxonMobil provides customers and commercial markets in the region with ground transportation, industrial, aviation and marine fuels, lubricants, petrochemicals and liquefied natural gas (LNG).

As Singapore serves as the AP hub for some of our businesses, we employ about 3,500 people across positions in operations, projects, commercial, corporate support functions and others.

This is an exciting time to join our growing trading team and be an integral part of ExxonMobil.

title: Forward Deployment Engineer
description:
About the Role

This is a hands-on technical role at the intersection of product and customer deployments. You'll sit at the core of a fast-moving AI communication platform — owning end-to-end production rollouts, building integrations, and ensuring customers get reliable, real-world results from day one. Your work will directly shape how the product evolves by feeding field learnings back into engineering and product teams.

The company is a well-funded, seed-stage European startup building AI phone assistants for small and medium-sized businesses. The team is lean (~50 people) and growing rapidly, with a strong engineering culture and a proprietary orchestration layer built in-house with a focus on European data privacy standards.

What You'll Do

  • Act as the technical bridge between product and customer setups — translating business requirements into robust, production-ready implementations.

  • Lead end-to-end rollouts of AI assistant configurations in production, including workflows, logic, data flows, prompts, and guardrails.

  • Implement integrations with third-party systems via APIs and webhooks, covering CRMs, calendars, ticketing, payments, and common auth patterns (OAuth, API keys).

  • Develop glue code and small-to-medium features with tests, monitoring, and logging to map customer use cases to production systems.

  • Debug live issues across calls, flows, and data pipelines — and ship rapid fixes under production conditions.

  • Build reusable templates, deployment playbooks, and best practices to make setups scalable and repeatable across customers.

  • Maintain a tight feedback loop with product and engineering by surfacing pain points, feature gaps, and recurring patterns with concrete recommendations.

  • Own deployment success and ensure customer setups function reliably in live production call environments.

What We're Looking For

Must-haves:

  • 3+ years of experience in deployment engineering, delivering production AI integrations and automation workflows.

title: Associate Director, Data Product & AI Portfolio Lead - 24 Month FTC
description:
Are you ready to turn trusted data and agentic AI into measurable impact for patients and the business? This role leads the strategy and delivery of AI-ready data products, AI tools, agents, and orchestration across operations and supply chain, enabling faster, safer, and more insightful decisions. Based in Cork (Alexion Office) or Dublin (College Park), you will guide how data and AI assets are designed, governed, and reused to power automation and decision-making at scale. You will operate at the intersection of business, technology, and compliance—owning product direction, embedding responsible AI, and making sure our solutions are trusted, secure, explainable, and fit-for-purpose. Can you set a bold vision and convert it into pragmatic roadmaps teams can deliver against? Do you thrive in complexity and know how to simplify it for action? Your work will translate priorities into reusable data assets, governed AI products, agentic workflows, and outcomes that matter for colleagues and, ultimately, for patients.

Accountabilities: Strategy and Vision: Define and evolve the strategy for AI-ready data products and AI assets in priority domains, grounded in business value and customer needs, and translate these into product designs and iterative delivery plans.

Governance and Responsible AI: Operationalize governance standards for AI products, tools, agents, and orchestration, aligned to business value, risk appetite, regulatory expectations, and enterprise AI principles.

Roadmaps and Delivery: Create and maintain product roadmaps; lead delivery from inception to maturity with clear milestones, KPIs, and value realization. Backlog Ownership: Own and prioritize feature backlogs; partner with architects, analysts, and engineers to elaborate requirements and drive timely reversal of technical debt.

Lifecycle Governance: Participate in enterprise governance from idea intake and prioritization through design, build, validation, deployment, monitoring, change control, and retirement.

AI Readiness: Lead all aspects of AI readiness assessments for data products and business processes, including data quality, metadata completeness, lineage, access controls, model suitability, timely quality, human-in-the-loop requirements, and operational adoption readiness.

Quality and Assurance: Define quality and assurance criteria for AI-enabled solutions—performance, accuracy, reliability, explainability, bias and fairness, privacy, security, auditability—and ensure ongoing monitoring for drift or degradation. FAIR by Design: Champion agile, iterative development while ensuring data products are Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR). Release and Dependency Management: Handle cross-release dependencies to land phases and landmarks predictably. Collaborator Influence: Communicate clearly with leaders whose operations are impacted; align on value, readiness, and change plans.

Voice of the Business: Serve as the business voice to focus teams on what matters most and enable enterprise objectives. Documentation and Controls: Own and maintain business metadata, use-case documentation, decision records, risk assessments, control evidence, and quality metrics for specified data and AI products.

Agentic AI Operations: Partner with technical teams to ensure AI agents and orchestration workflows have clear ownership, guardrails, escalation paths, monitoring, and measurable value outcomes before production use. Data Stewardship: Perform Data Stewardship activities where assigned to ensure integrity, access, and reusability.

Impact Progression: Deliver immediate value through prioritized features and readiness improvements; scale impact by maturing governance, accelerating reuse, and enabling trusted automation across multiple functions.

Essential Skills/Experience: -

Experience governing data products and/or AI-enabled products across the lifecycle, with the ability to translate business priorities into practical standards, controls, and adoption pathways.

- Thrives in a fast-paced work environment, comfortable with complexity and uncertainty at times, dedication to deliver outcomes and motivated by the opportunity to rethink our approach to healthcare.

- Ability to handle a cross-functional product development and deployment process, including teams of people with diverse skills to perform the needed tasks

- Comfortable operating in a heavily matrixed organizations with excellent communication skills and intuition to handle the needs of various stakeholders. - Solid Project and / or Product management skills, including handling budgets, timelines and risks.

- Experience bringing innovation to bear on solving complex and multi-dimensional issues from an operational, technical, financial and human perspective. - Understanding of AI product governance principles, including responsible AI, AI risk management, model and prompt evaluation, human oversight, explainability, monitoring, and lifecycle documentation.

- Deep familiarity with data engineering concepts such as ETL, data modelling, data lakes / databases, reference data, master data, etc.

- Experience leading or working on agile development teams - Excellent leadership, communication, influencing, and collaborator management skills

- Experience establishing, communicating, and delivering product roadmaps - Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with the ability to make data-driven decisions - Ability to rapidly grasp concepts and to handle complexity by simplifying it for others and providing clear directions to delivery teams.

- Familiarity with AI readiness requirements for high-quality AI outcomes, including trusted data foundations, metadata, lineage, access controls, privacy, security, data quality, and reuse standards.

- Ability to collaborate with data scientists, AI engineers, product teams, architects, compliance partners, and business collaborators to define requirements and quality expectations for AI tools, agents, and orchestration workflows

- Ability to handle and influence strategically and persuade tactfully, to obtain desired outcomes while maintaining effective, positive, organizational relationships.

Desirable Skills/Experience:

- Master’s or PhD in a scientific or technical rigor. - 5+ years of relevant experience in pharmaceutical industry with strong knowledge of Drug Development Processes and the diverse sources of information that support, inform and assist in healthcare/clinical research.

- Familiarity with the latest research and thinking and understanding of dynamics affecting the pharmaceutical industry and needs for transformation

. - Familiarity with data science, data visualization, and reporting concepts - Ability to work in fast-paced, dynamic environment and handle multiple streams of work simultaneously

- Experience with generative AI, AI agents, agentic orchestration, MLOps/LLMOps, AI assurance, model governance, or responsible AI frameworks would be advantageous.

Why AstraZeneca: Here, meaningful science meets entrepreneurial energy. You will feel the pace and autonomy of a leading biotech environment backed by the scale, investment, and rigor of a global biopharma. We bring unexpected teams into the same room—engineers, product leaders, clinicians, and compliance experts—to unleash bold thinking rooted in patient need. Our culture values kindness alongside ambition, so you can take ownership, learn fast, and stretch your craft while staying grounded in integrity and responsibility. Your contribution will help transform how data and AI guide critical decisions for people living with devastating and often overlooked conditions, turning everyday work into progress that truly counts.

title: Quality Control Inspector II
description:
Job Summary

The Quality Control Inspector II is responsible for performing inspections of incoming materials, in-process components, and finished products to ensure compliance with customer specifications, engineering drawings, company standards, and regulatory requirements. This position utilizes precision measuring equipment, interprets technical documentation, supports quality system activities, and assists in identifying and resolving quality issues. The Quality Control Inspector II serves as a resource to production personnel and may assist in training less experienced inspectors.

Essential Job Functions

  • Perform incoming, in-process, first article, and final inspections in accordance with established procedures and quality standards.
  • Verify product conformity using precision measuring instruments, gauges, and inspection equipment.
  • Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, specifications, and customer requirements
  • Accurately document inspection, testing, and measurement results.
  • Identify and document nonconforming product and ensure proper segregation and disposition.
  • Support root cause investigations and corrective action activities for quality issues.
  • Maintain inspection records and controlled documentation in accordance with quality system requirements.
  • Verify calibration status of measuring and test equipment prior to use and assist with calibration record maintenance.
  • Monitor production processes to ensure compliance with established quality standards.
  • Communicate quality concerns and inspection results to production, engineering, and management teams.
  • Participate in internal audits and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Assist in preparing and reviewing First Article Inspection (FAI) documentation.
  • Train and mentor Quality Control Inspector I personnel as assigned.
  • Maintain a safe and organized work environment.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

    Education and Experience

    • High School Diploma or GED required.
    • Associate degree in a technical or manufacturing-related field preferred.
    • Minimum of two (2) to four (4) years of quality inspection experience in a manufacturing environment.
    • Aerospace manufacturing experience preferred.
    • AS9102 First Article Inspection experience preferred
    • Visual acuity, color recognition, and depth perception necessary to perform inspection functions
    • Strong understanding of inspection techniques and quality assurance principles.
    • Working knowledge of ISO 9001 and AS9100 quality management systems.
    • Proficiency in the use of calipers, micrometers, height gauges, optical comparators, and other measuring devices.
    • Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings and GD&T preferred.
    • Ability to prioritize work and meet deadlines in a fast-paced manufacturing environment
    • Proficient with Microsoft Office applications and quality documentation systems.
    • Experience with ERP systems, calibration systems, or similar quality systems preferred

title: Rostering Assistant
description:
Job Description

Overview

AtkinsRéalis is seeking a highly organised and proactive Rostering Assistant to support the effective planning, coordination and deployment of resources across the Practice. Working within a fast-paced operational environment, you will play a key role in administering the Fatigue 360 system, supporting workforce planning activities, and ensuring roster, travel and accommodation requirements are delivered efficiently and compliantly.

Working closely with managers, employees and external suppliers, you will help ensure the right resources are available at the right time to meet operational and project requirements while maintaining high standards of service, compliance and operational excellence.

Your role

  • Act as the key administrator for the Fatigue 360 system, ensuring all employee records are accurately established, maintained and updated, and that rosters align with operational and project requirements whilst maintaining compliance with relevant policies and standards.
  • Manage and administer Fatigue 360 across the Practice, monitoring fatigue and associated risks, proactively liaising with employees and managers to identify issues and implement appropriate actions where required.
  • Produce and distribute roster, fatigue and compliance reports from Fatigue 360 in line with Terms & Conditions, management reporting requirements and operational needs.
  • Coordinate and allocate resources effectively to maximise workforce productivity and operational efficiency, supporting workforce planning activities to ensure the right resources are available at the right time to meet business and client requirements.
  • Plan, arrange and communicate accommodation and travel requirements for employees, ensuring practical, timely and cost-effective solutions are delivered to support operational delivery.
  • Provide support and guidance to managers and employees on roster management, fatigue compliance and workforce planning activities, delivering a high level of customer service and responding promptly to workforce planning, travel and accommodation queries.
  • Monitor staffing levels and resource availability, identifying potential resource gaps and supporting contingency planning. Maintain accurate workforce planning records and provide management information, reporting and analysis to support decision-making.

About you

  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and the ability to maintain accurate records, produce reports and manage multiple tasks effectively.

You will be self-motivated, reliable, professional and adaptable, with strong problem-solving skills, a collaborative approach, and confidence engaging with a wide range of stakeholders. Clinical Safety Leadership

  • Lead initiatives for process improvement and cross-departmental process consistency

Portfolio Management Expertise

description:
Introduction


A career in IBM Consulting is built on long-term client relationships and close collaboration worldwide. You’ll work with leading companies across industries, helping them shape their hybrid cloud and AI journeys. With support from our strategic partners, robust IBM technology, and Red Hat, you’ll have the tools to drive meaningful change and accelerate client impact. Our culture of growth and empathy focuses on your long-term career development while valuing your unique skills and experiences.


Your Role And Responsibilities


As a Data Engineer specializing in Data Integration, you will design and build solutions to transfer data from operational and external environments to the business intelligence environment. You will utilize various tools to create and implement Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) processes, ensuring the seamless flow of data throughout the business intelligence solution's lifecycle.


Your Primary Responsibilities Will Include



  • Design Data Integration Solutions: Create solutions to transfer data from operational and external environments to the business intelligence environment, utilizing tools such as Informatica, Ab Initio software, and DataStage.

  • Ensure Seamless Data Flow: Ensure the smooth flow of data throughout the business intelligence solution's lifecycle by creating and implementing efficient ETL processes.

  • Support Business Intelligence: Support the business intelligence environment by designing and building solutions to transfer data from operational and external environments.


Required Technical And Professional Expertise



  • Strong hands-on experience in ETL development using Informatica PowerCenter.

  • Proficient in writing and optimizing complex SQL queries.

  • Experience working with relational databases.

  • Ability to build, maintain, and troubleshoot ETL pipelines.

  • Strong understanding of data accuracy, consistency, and reliability.

  • Capable of identifying and resolving data and performance issues.

  • Ability to work independently and deliver reliable data solutions.

  • Good communication skills to collaborate with stakeholders and understand data requirements.

description:
About the Role

We're a small, ambitious team building applied AI systems at the intersection of private market investing and cutting-edge model capabilities. This is an early- to mid-career role for a software engineer who wants to own production systems end to end — shipping agent-powered features, full-stack applications, and durable workflows that turn improving model capabilities into dependable, economically valuable tools.

You'll work in person with a tight-knit team in San Francisco, take on substantial ownership from day one, and help shape both the technical foundation and engineering culture of a high-conviction company backed by top-tier investors.

Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

What You'll Do

  • Build and operate production systems spanning agent architectures, full-stack applications, durable workflows, and data infrastructure.

  • Own system design, deployment, and iteration for agent-powered features from concept to production.

  • Evaluate new models, frameworks, tool-use patterns, and context strategies — then productionize the improvements that matter.

  • Build evaluation pipelines, observability tooling, and human-review systems to make agent behavior measurable and reliable.

  • Develop durable workflows and data infrastructure covering tool coordination, context management, state, retries, and failure recovery.

  • Design and implement interfaces that make complex agent workflows clear, fast, and intuitive for end users.

  • Lead substantial cross-functional projects across product, agents, data, and infrastructure — and receive direct user feedback on your work.

  • Contribute meaningfully to engineering culture and technical direction on a small, high-ownership team.

What We're Looking For

Required:

  • A few years of software engineering experience with strong fundamentals and a proven track record of shipping production systems.

  • Hands-on experience building and operating human-in-the-loop evaluation and review systems to monitor and improve agent behavior.

  • Strong ownership mindset with demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional projects across product, data, and infrastructure.

  • Experience building full-stack applications and owning features end to end.

  • Direct experience with LLM applications, agents, tool use, or other applied AI systems.

  • High agency, strong product judgment, and comfort moving fluidly across product, backend, data, and infrastructure.

  • Genuine curiosity about agent developments and the judgment to separate useful advances from hype.

  • Based in San Francisco or excited to relocate — this role is fully in-person.

Nice to Have:

  • Background in fintech, financial data, or capital markets.

  • Experience at early-stage startups.

  • Hands-on work with durable workflow orchestration (e.g., Temporal, Prefect, or similar).

  • Experience handling sensitive or permissioned data.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary: $150,000 – $250,000 USD annually, depending on experience.

  • Equity participation in a well-backed, early-stage company.

  • Direct impact on a small team where your work is immediately visible and consequential.

Location

This role is on-site in San Francisco, CA. Candidates must be based locally or genuinely willing to relocate. Remote work is not available for this position.

title: Product Engineer (Full-Stack / Agentic AI)
description:
About the Role

A well-funded European PropTech company building an AI-native operating system for short-term and holiday rental management is looking for a Product Engineer to join a lean, high-impact team. You'll design and ship agentic AI systems that observe, decide, and act on real-world property operations — with humans in the loop. This is a central, full-ownership role: you'll modernise legacy systems, redesign data structures, and turn messy operational workflows into reliable, autonomous software.

What You'll Do

  • Own features end-to-end — from requirement gathering through to production-ready shipping.

  • Design and build agentic AI workflows covering guest communication (chat and voice), operational decisions, and property tasks.

  • Modernise legacy systems and redesign data structures to meet evolving product requirements.

  • Shadow real operational workflows to surface inefficiencies, hidden steps, and workarounds.

  • Translate complex, messy processes into clean, scalable software.

  • Scope, ship, and iterate — driving solutions independently rather than working from a ticket queue.

  • Collaborate closely with internal teams to keep product and engineering aligned.

  • Operate with high agency and ownership, delivering results rapidly and safely.

What We're Looking For

Required:

  • Demonstrable engineering experience you can show during the hiring process.

  • Strong TypeScript skills — this is a firm requirement.

  • Proven ability to own features end-to-end: from gathering requirements to shipping production software.

  • Track record of shipping quickly with sound judgement about what can safely break.

  • Familiarity with React, Express, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and AWS; comfortable using Linear and Notion for tracking and documentation.

  • Comfort working in an agentic engineering style — e.g. running multiple agents, parallel terminals, and AI coding assistants.

  • Strong product taste: attention to user experience down to messaging and interaction wording.

  • Ability to self-manage: plan work, communicate progress, and flag blockers proactively.

  • Fluent English and strong written/verbal communication skills.

  • Willingness to relocate to Germany and work from the Berlin office periodically.

Nice to Have:

  • Founder mentality or prior startup founding experience.

title: Associate Director, Quality Control
description:
This is what you will do:

The management and oversight of the following QC activities: analytical, microbiological; sample management; direct laboratory testing support; equipment management & maintenance support to ensure fully compliant, effective and safe Quality Control laboratories. The compliance and inspection readiness of all Quality Control activities on site and in line with regulatory and quality standards related to the testing of Alexion products per respective licensed specifications, as well as technical support of new products, registrations, filings.

Lead and support QC forums and provide technical expertise in support of the Alexion Athlone operational functions & network.

You will be responsible for:

· Provide leadership and oversight to the QC laboratory functions, ensuring the full application, implementation, and adherence to current testing standards as well as EHS standards, maintaining effective, compliant, and safe QC laboratories in accordance with GMP and EAEU requirements.

· Accountable for review, approval, or rejection of all raw materials, packaging materials, intermediates, bulk, and finished products, by ensuring these meet approved specifications and quality standards before release, use, or distribution.

· Accountable for review and approval of all QC-related specifications, sampling procedures, test methods, instructions, and procedures, ensuring their suitability, relevance, and regulatory compliance prior to implementation or update.

· Ensure the establishment, validation/qualification, calibration, and routine maintenance of all QC equipment and laboratory systems, in accordance with internal and regulatory requirements, to support accurate and reliable testing.

· Oversee and ensure the formal recording, review, evaluation, and retention of all QC test data, guaranteeing data integrity, traceability, and readiness for internal and regulatory audits.

· Monitor and control QC testing processes, ensuring adherence to agreed lead times and compliance with approved methods and specifications.

· Provide QC review and formal approval on relevant QC documentation, as required, to support the release of pharmaceutical materials and products in compliance with regulatory expectations.

· Implement, communicate, and continuously maintain all QC Standards, Procedures, and GMP documentation, ensuring ongoing compliance, continuous improvement, and readiness for inspection.

· Ensure standardized QC practices and systems across all site QC functions and champion the implementation of Operational Excellence principles, including Continuous Improvement and Digital Strategy.

· Represent the QC function at regulatory, corporate, and internal inspections, audits, and quality forums, ensuring all QC-related requirements are understood and demonstrated.

· Oversee the recruitment, development, and retention of all QC staff, ensuring suitable training, qualification, and competency management to deliver a flexible and robust QC workforce.

· Lead the local design and execution of the global QC strategy and deployment, ensuring alignment with corporate objectives and compliance standards.

· Establish and maintain effective communication and networking with Quality professionals, both internally and externally, to ensure the ongoing application of evolving Quality Laboratory standards and regulatory requirements.

You will need to have:

· A minimum of 15 years’ experience in a pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical company in roles with increasing responsibility in quality leadership

· BSc in Biochemistry, Chemistry, Microbiology or other life sciences. An advanced degree (MSc/PhD) is an advantage

· Extensive GMP laboratory/Quality management within a multi-national pharma/biopharma company is essential.

· Proven ability to build, mentor and grow agile high performing teams

· Knowledge of business and management principles involved in resource allocation, financial management, leadership and co-ordination of people and resources.

· Proven ability to work in a matrixed organization

· Extensive experience of the all regulatory requirements associated with QC methods, submissions & variations

We would prefer for you to have:

· Experience in a leadership role within a biopharmaceutical company.

· Skilled in organisation, planning and priority setting.

· Previous experience in handling regulatory audits and inspections.

· Experience working in a global and diverse work environment.

title: Director, Commercial REMS Operations - Pharmaceutical
location: Boston, Massachusetts, United States of America
description:
Director, Commercial REMS Operations

Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease
Location: Boston, MA (Seaport) preferred

alternate: New Haven, CT

Do you have expertise in REMS strategy, operations, and cross-functional commercial collaboration?

At Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease, we are united by a mission to transform the lives of people affected by rare diseases. Here, your work has the potential to shape meaningful outcomes for patients while influencing how we deliver compliant, efficient, and scalable commercial support across complex therapeutic areas.

We are seeking a Director of Commercial REMS Operations to lead key strategies and tactics supporting US Commercial activities related to Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) programs. This is a highly visible role where you will help drive the development, implementation, and ongoing management of REMS initiatives across US Commercial, ensuring alignment, operational excellence, and continued focus on patient safety.

What You'll Do

As Director, Commercial REMS Operations, you will lead the commercial strategy, execution, and continuous improvement of REMS programs across Alexion and AstraZeneca's rare disease portfolio. Serving as the primary Commercial REMS leader, you will partner with Commercial, Sales Operations, Commercial Enablement, Patient Services, Regulatory, Safety, Ethics & Compliance, IT, and external vendors to ensure REMS requirements support both compliance and business success. You will be accountable for Commercial REMS strategy and execution, serving as the primary REMS leader until escalation to the Senior Director.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead Commercial REMS strategy, operational execution, governance, and performance across products and indications.
  • Partner with field teams, sales operations, commercial enablement, and patient services organizations to strengthen REMS education, awareness, and execution.
  • Translate REMS requirements into scalable business processes, field capabilities, communications, and training strategies.
  • Drive data-informed decision making through reporting, analytics, performance monitoring, and business insights.
  • Serve as the Commercial lead for REMS data strategy, governance, quality, and reporting.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives that improve REMS effectiveness, compliance, stakeholder experience, and operational efficiency.
  • Oversee vendors supporting REMS operations, analytics, technology, and reporting solutions.
  • Support launch readiness, new REMS initiatives, and ongoing program optimization.
  • Present risks, opportunities, and strategic recommendations to senior leadership.

Why This Role Matters

This role sits at the intersection of Commercial Strategy, Field Execution, Data Analytics, and Compliance. Success requires a leader who can balance regulatory requirements with business needs, leverage data to drive decisions, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and ensure REMS programs effectively support both patient safety and commercial success.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related discipline.
  • 7+ years of experience supporting REMS programs within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
  • Demonstrated commercial experience supporting a product with an active FDA REMS program.
  • Experience partnering directly with cross-functional Commercial leadership, Sales Operations, Field Enablement, Commercial Excellence, Patient Services, Market Access, Analytics, and Medical Affairs teams.
  • Proven experience leading REMS strategy, operational execution, and cross-functional governance within a complex matrix environment.
  • Strong understanding of FDA REMS requirements, compliance obligations, assessment activities, and ongoing program optimization.
  • Experience translating regulatory requirements into effective commercial processes, field education strategies, and operational solutions.
  • Advanced analytical capabilities with experience leveraging data to evaluate REMS effectiveness, identify business risks, inform decision-making, and drive continuous improvement.
  • Experience managing external vendors and holding third-party partners accountable for operational execution, performance metrics, and compliance standards.
  • Strong leadership, stakeholder management, and executive communication skills with the ability to influence across multiple functions and organizational levels.
  • Demonstrated success managing multiple strategic initiatives simultaneously while delivering measurable business outcomes.

Preferred Requirements

  • Master’s degree in business administration, Public Health, Data Science, Life Sciences, or a related field.
  • Experience supporting launch products requiring REMS design, implementation, or commercialization readiness activities.
  • Experience working in high-growth, rapidly evolving commercial organizations.
  • Knowledge of commercial data ecosystems, data governance practices, and healthcare data management principles.
  • Experience overseeing vendors responsible for data engineering, reporting, automation, or analytics solutions.
  • Exposure to Snowflake, SQL, Python, R, or other data and analytics technologies.
  • Experience working with commercial dashboards, reporting platforms, or advanced data visualization tools.
  • Experience supporting REMS-related field communications, sales training initiatives, or commercial capability-building programs.
  • Experience leading vendor governance, budget oversight, contract management, and performance review processes.

Why join us?

At Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease, you will be part of a team driven by science, urgency, and purpose. We are committed to pushing boundaries for patients with rare diseases, and we know that achieving this takes exceptional people, strong collaboration, and a culture where different perspectives are welcomed.

This is an opportunity to take on a strategic and impactful role at the intersection of commercial operations, compliance, data, and patient safety. You will work across a wide stakeholder network, help shape how REMS programs are delivered, and contribute to the success of both current and future products.

Location strategy

This position may be in either Boston, MA (Seaport) or New Haven, CT, depending on business needs and candidate preference. AstraZeneca follows a hybrid working model, with employees expected to be onsite at least three days per week in their assigned location. Candidates must possess the legal right to work in the relevant country; work visa eligibility and/or sponsorship requirements will be considered in accordance with local regulations. Remote work is not offered.

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace, and challenge perceptions. That’s why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that doesn’t mean we’re not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility. Join us in our unique and ambitious world.

Pay transparency

The annual base pay for this position could range from $215,693 – $260,000 USD Annual. Hourly and salaried non-exempt employees will also be paid overtime pay when working qualifying overtime hours. Base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. In addition, our positions offer a short-term incentive bonus opportunity; eligibility to participate in our equity-based long-term incentive program (salaried roles), to receive a retirement contribution (hourly roles), and commission payment eligibility (sales roles). Benefits offered include a qualified retirement program [401(k) plan]; paid vacation and holidays; paid leaves; and health benefits including medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision coverage in accordance with the terms and conditions of the applicable plans. Additional details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment. If hired, employees will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base pay (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors.

title: Tools Developer/Hardware Engineer
description:
Fluence (Nasdaq: FLNC) is a global market leader delivering intelligent energy storage and optimization software for renewables and storage. Our solutions and operational services are helping to create a more resilient grid and unlock the full potential of renewable portfolios. With gigawatts of successful implementations across nearly 50 markets, we are transforming the way we power our world for a more sustainable future. For more information, please visit fluenceenergy.com.

Job Description:

Role Overview

Fluence is seeking a Tools Developer to strengthen its Americas Services organization by designing and developing tools that improve fleet observability, troubleshooting efficiency, proactive monitoring, and operational reliability across Fluence's Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) fleet.

This role sits at the intersection of Software Development, Linux System Administration, Operational Technology (OT), Service Engineering, and Fleet Reliability. The successful candidate will develop software solutions, monitoring frameworks, automation tools, and diagnostic platforms that enable early detection of hardware and software issues, improve root cause analysis, and reduce customer downtime.

The ideal candidate combines strong Python development capabilities with hands-on experience supporting Linux/Ubuntu environments, Distributed Access Systems (DAS), OS7 platforms, Grafana dashboards, operational monitoring systems, and industrial control networks.

This position directly supports customer satisfaction, fleet reliability, service scalability, and operational excellence throughout North and South America.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain software tools that improve fleet monitoring, troubleshooting efficiency, and operational reliability across Fluence's Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) fleet
  • Develop applications, automation scripts, and diagnostic tools that support Service Engineering, Fleet Optimization, Technical Support, and Field Service organizations.
  • Create proactive hardware and software monitoring solutions that identify system issues before they impact customer operations.
  • Design, develop, and maintain Grafana dashboards, visualizations, and alerting frameworks to improve fleet observability, troubleshooting, and operational decision-making.
  • Work with the digital team, creating requirements for Nispera, Alerta, and Zabbix tooling.
  • Develop monitoring and diagnostic tools supporting Data Acquisition Systems (DAS), OS7 environments, Linux servers, network infrastructure, and edge computing systems.
  • Build automation capabilities that reduce manual troubleshooting effort and accelerate identification of hardware failures, software issues, communication faults, and network disruptions.
  • Develop tools that collect, process, analyze, and present operational data from multiple fleet systems and monitoring platforms.
  • Support root cause analysis efforts through development of automated diagnostic workflows and troubleshooting utilities.
  • Collaborate with Controls & SCADA Engineers, Network Support Engineers, Product Engineering, Deployment Teams, and Field Service Engineers to develop scalable solutions addressing operational challenges.
  • Support fleet reliability initiatives by identifying opportunities for automation, process improvement, and proactive issue detection.
  • Maintain software documentation, system architecture documentation, deployment procedures, and operational support materials.
  • Assist with critical customer escalations by developing tools and diagnostics that improve troubleshooting accuracy.
  • Serve as the primary technical resource for complex hardware-related issues across Fluence's operational Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) fleet.
  • Review and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, assembly drawings, and hardware documentation to diagnose and resolve field issues.
  • Collaborate with Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Network Solutions Deployment (NSD), and Field Service teams to identify and resolve hardware design issues discovered during deployment and operations.
  • Support fleet-wide hardware upgrade initiatives by developing implementation plans, validating compatibility, identifying risks, and supporting execution.
  • Evaluate recurring hardware failures and identify opportunities for product improvements, reliability enhancements, and corrective actions.
  • Support technical investigations involving hardware non-conformances, field failures, warranty claims, and customer escalations.
  • Develop troubleshooting procedures, repair instructions, hardware service bulletins, and technical documentation to improve field support capabilities.
  • Provide technical guidance and escalation support to Field Service Engineers, Technical Support teams, and Customer Operations organizations.
  • Support spare parts planning and lifecycle management by identifying critical components, obsolescence risks, replacement strategies, and alternate part solutions.
  • Analyze failure trends across the installed fleet and work with engineering teams to drive corrective and preventive actions.
  • Participate in Root Cause Analysis (RCA) activities and Lessons Learned reviews to improve fleet reliability and reduce repeat issues.
  • Support factory acceptance testing, site commissioning activities, and post-deployment investigations when hardware performance concerns arise.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical field.
  • 5+ years of experience in software development, automation, systems engineering, observability platforms, or operational technology environments.
  • Proficiency in Python development, including scripting, automation, data processing, and application development.
  • Hands-on experience administering and troubleshooting Linux and Ubuntu operating systems.
  • Experience developing monitoring, troubleshooting, diagnostic, or observability tools in production environments.
  • Experience with Grafana dashboard creation, data visualization, and alert management.
  • Experience working with REST APIs, data integrations, and automation frameworks.
  • Strong understanding of networking fundamentals, communication protocols, and system diagnostics.
  • Experience with Git and software development lifecycle best practices.
  • Excellent troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams.
  • Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience supporting utility-scale Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS).
  • Experience with OS7 environments and associated operational technologies.
  • Experience supporting or developing solutions for Distributed Access Systems (DAS).
  • Experience with industrial networking, SCADA systems, PLC communications, or operational technology (OT) environments.
  • Experience with Modbus communications, telemetry systems, and edge computing platforms.
  • Experience working in customer-facing service organizations supporting critical infrastructure.
  • Knowledge of Docker, containerized applications, virtualization technologies, and cloud-hosted monitoring environments.
  • Experience with SQL, time-series databases, and large-scale data analytics.
  • Experience building fleet-wide monitoring, observability, and predictive maintenance solutions.
  • Familiarity with cybersecurity principles and secure system deployment practices.
  • Experience supporting global or multi-regional operational environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver scalable tools that improve fleet reliability, customer uptime, and operational efficiency.

In compliance with California pay transparency regulations, the base salary range for this position is $126,000-$158,000+ per year. Final compensation will depend on experience and qualifications.

Our Culture

At Fluence, our culture is the foundation that drives our ambitious growth strategy and fuels our mission to transform the future of energy. Our core cultural pillars empower us to innovate, collaborate, and lead with purpose, ensuring we continue to deliver unparalleled value to our customers and the world.

Unleash Voices

We believe every voice matters. We encourage openness, active listening, and decisive action to create a culture where everyone has the opportunity to contribute to our success. We foster an environment where diverse perspectives are heard and valued, driving innovation and progress.

Customer Fluent

Our customers are at the heart of everything we do. We’re committed to delivering exceptional value that exceeds expectations by understanding our customers' needs and adapting swiftly to meet them. Our deep focus on customer satisfaction drives us to continuously improve and innovate.

Infinite Impact

We are committed to creating the impossible. We push boundaries to deliver sustainable, game-changing solutions that shape a brighter, more energy-efficient future for all. Our team is passionate about making a lasting impact that will resonate for generations to come.

All In

We are all in for growth. Our teams are relentlessly focused on identifying and seizing opportunities that propel us forward. We embrace an ownership mindset, pushing ourselves and each other to accelerate progress and create lasting success.

Equal Opportunity Employer
At Fluence, we believe great teams are built on a collaborative and connected culture. We’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and welcome qualified applicants of all backgrounds. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, gender identity or expression, genetic information, or any other status protected by law.

Work Authorization
To join our team, you’ll need to be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and throughout your employment, without the need for employer sponsorship. Please note that Fluence does not sponsor work visas for this position.

title: Information Systems Security Officer
description:
The Digital Modernization Sector at Leidos currently pursuing a new opportunity that has openings for a Information System Security Officer (ISSO) to work in Tampa, FL. This is an exciting opportunity to use your experience helping the U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) Enterprise Development, Application, and Training (EDAT) mission. In this mission we are focused on providing innovative, data-driven solutions and enterprise architecture enhancements to enable seamless operations across USSOCOM's global network. The program emphasizes rapid development and deployment of technologies to enhance the mobility and readiness of Special Operations Forces (SOF) in both combat and non-combat scenarios. Key tasks include program management, application development, training support, and technology integration to maintain USSOCOM's operational edge. The EDAT program underscores agility and adaptability, ensuring SOF professionals have access to the information and tools they need to meet evolving mission requirements.


Primary Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the lead Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO) embedded with a software development team, ensuring that all cybersecurity compliance requirements are met throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) for Azure-based portal and gateway applications.

  • Guide the development team in interpreting and applying DoD cybersecurity policies, NIST RMF guidance, and DISA STIG requirements throughout system development and deployment.

  • Ensure full compliance with applicable security frameworks, including the NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF), FedRAMP, and the DISA Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide (SRG).

  • Own and maintain key security documentation such as the System Security Plan (SSP), Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M), Security Assessment Report (SAR), and supporting artifacts required for achieving and sustaining an Authority to Operate (ATO).

  • Coordinate closely with Authorizing Officials (AOs), Information System Security Managers (ISSMs), system owners, and other stakeholders to manage and drive the ATO process across multiple classification levels.

  • Provide oversight and direction for the integration of enterprise cybersecurity services (e.g., ACAS, HBSS, BCAP, PKI/ICAM) and ensure these services are properly accounted for in security documentation and compliance testing.

  • Monitor and assess system vulnerabilities and audit results; ensure findings are documented and tracked to closure in accordance with policy.

  • Experience mentoring junior cybersecurity personnel and fostering a compliance-driven security culture within cross-functional teams.

  • Knowledge of emerging cybersecurity technologies and their implications for DoD cloud security compliance.

  • Participate in Agile and Waterfall development meetings to provide governance input and security policy guidance that aligns with DoD accreditation expectations.

  • Stay informed of changes in DoD cybersecurity guidance, threat landscape developments, and cloud security best practices to adjust compliance strategies as needed.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Assurance, or related discipline and 12 years of relevant experience, or a Master’s degree with 8 years of relevant experience.

  • Active Top Secret security clearance.

  • Relevant certifications such as Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Authorization Professional (CAP), or CompTIA Advanced Security Practitioner (CASP+).

  • Demonstrated knowledge of the NIST RMF, eMASS workflows, and DoD cloud accreditation processes.

  • The ability to work through complex problems using applied technical knowledge, understanding, reasoning and interpretation.

  • Proven experience managing security compliance for cloud-hosted solutions in Azure or similar environments.

  • Strong understanding of DISA STIGs, NIST 800-53 controls, and vulnerability management processes.

  • Familiarity with DevSecOps and Agile SDLC methodologies from a governance and compliance oversight perspective.

  • Has in-depth understanding of technical principles, theories, concepts and their application across range of programs.

  • Proven success in liaising with AOs, ISSMs, and system owners to navigate and expedite RMF-based accreditation efforts.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to brief complex security concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelors degree Computer IS Systems, Cybersecurity, Information Assurance, or a related field and 12+ years of prior relevant experience as an ISSO or in a similar cybersecurity compliance oversight role supporting DoD systems or a Masters degree in Information Technology or related field and 10 years of prior relevant experience in cybersecurity compliance.

  • Familiarity with supporting systems at multiple classification levels (e.g., Unclassified, Secret).

description:
